source_text: Si divinas litteras credimus, non ut fabulae sed ut disciplinae scriptae sunt. Induratio Pharaonis non Deum auctorem mali facit, sed iudicium revelat. Sol iustos illuminat, lutum indurat — eadem operatio diversos effectus.
pass_a_gloss: If divine letters we-believe, not as fables but as disciplines written they-are. Hardening of-Pharaoh not God author of-evil makes, but judgment reveals. Sun righteous illuminates, mud hardens — same operation diverse effects.
pass_b_english: If we believe these letters divine, they are written for our training, not as antique gossip. Hardening does not make God the author of evil; it discloses judgment. The same sun softens wax and hardens mud: one working, different effects according to the matter that receives it.
